# Source: /core-concepts/tables/event-tables

---
draft: false
title: Event Tables
description: Declare event tables and subscribe to event-table streams safely.
sidebar:
  order: 7
---

<a class="upstream-doc" href="https://spacetimedb.com/docs/tables/event-tables" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">SpacetimeDB: Event Tables ↗</a>

Event tables use the same `Stdb.table(...)` builder with `event: true`.

```typescript
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"

const presenceEvent = Stdb.table("presenceEvent", {
  public: true,
  event: true,
  columns: {
    userId: Stdb.string(),
    kind: Stdb.literal("joined", "left"),
  },
})

const Module = Stdb.Module.make("presence", {}).addTables(presenceEvent)
const Example = Stdb.project(Module)

const program = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const session = yield* Example.client.ws.Session
  yield* session.streamEventTable("presenceEvent").pipe(
    Stream.runForEach((event) =>
      Effect.log(`presence ${event.row.userId} ${event.row.kind}`),
    ),
  )
})
```

effect-spacetimedb separates public persistent table targets
from public event-table targets in `Stdb.project(...).targets`. Use
`Example.targets.eventTables.presenceEvent` for direct target subscriptions and
`streamEventTable("presenceEvent")` for insert-only event streams.

Event tables use native delivery semantics: an event is delivered once for each
live native query set that covers it. If an application needs exactly one
event-processing path, subscribe once at the app state boundary and fan out from
that Effect stream or Atom rather than opening duplicate event-table streams in
several consumers.


---

# Source: /core-concepts/tables/file-storage

---
draft: false
title: File Storage
description: Mount the native files library and call its helpers from an Effect reducer.
sidebar:
  order: 9
---

Mount `@spacetimedb/files/submodule` to store files in the same database as your application. Install `@spacetimedb/files` alongside the SDK and ensure both resolve the same `spacetimedb/server` instance. Declare a type-only reference in the shared contract. The module entry supplies the actual library.

```ts title="files-contract.ts"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"

export const Drive = Stdb.Module.make("drive")
  .mountNative<typeof import("@spacetimedb/files/submodule")>()("files")
  .add(Stdb.Group.make("Uploads").add(
    Stdb.Fn.reducer("upload", {
      params: Stdb.struct({ bytes: Stdb.bytes() }),
    }),
  ))
```

This reducer stores an owner-visible file under the calling identity. The mounted native context omits `env`. The `@spacetimedb/files` 0.1.0 helper signature expects a full reducer context including `env`. Its upload helper uses fields available on the mounted alias. Keep the type assertion local to the helper call.

```ts title="files-server.ts"
import * as files from "@spacetimedb/files/submodule"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"
import { build } from "effect-spacetimedb/server-compiler"
import { Drive } from "./files-contract"

const uploads = Stdb.Builder.group(Drive, "Uploads", {
  upload: ({ bytes }) => Drive.mounts.files.use((ctx) =>
    files.uploadFile(ctx as files.FilesCtx, {
      path: "/attachment.bin",
      bytes: Array.from(bytes),
      mimeType: "application/octet-stream",
      visibility: files.FILE_VISIBILITY_OWNER,
    }, ctx.sender.toHexString()),
  ).pipe(Effect.asVoid),
})
const compiled = build(Drive, [
  uploads,
  Stdb.Builder.mountNative(Drive, "files", files),
])
export const ModuleExports = compiled.exportGroup()
export default compiled.schema
```

For a read procedure, use the same alias inside `Drive.withTx` and call `files.readFileBytes` with the path and authorized owner. The root module supplies any public routes and checks access before returning file contents. See [Submodules](/core-concepts/databases/submodules) and [SpacetimeDB File Storage](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/tables/file-storage).


---

# Source: /core-concepts/tables/indexes

---
draft: false
title: Indexes
description: Declare btree, hash, and direct indexes from table columns.
sidebar:
  order: 3
---

<a class="upstream-doc" href="https://spacetimedb.com/docs/tables/indexes" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">SpacetimeDB: Indexes ↗</a>

Single-column indexes can live on the column. Composite indexes live in the
table's `indexes` callback.

```typescript
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"

const playerScore = Stdb.table("playerScore", {
  public: true,
  columns: {
    id: Stdb.u64().primaryKey().autoInc(),
    playerId: Stdb.string().index("hash"),
    score: Stdb.u32().index("direct"),
    season: Stdb.string(),
  },
  indexes: (columns) => [
    Stdb.index("bySeasonScore", [
      columns.season,
      columns.score,
    ], { algorithm: "btree" }),
  ],
})
```

effect-spacetimedb accepts the native algorithms
`"btree"`, `"hash"`, and `"direct"` at both declaration sites. `hash` indexes
are point-only; `direct` indexes are range-capable.

## Indexable Column Types

`btree` and `hash` index any column type the host can key, including
`Stdb.enum(...)` and payload-carrying `Stdb.sum(...)` columns. A unit-variant
enum is keyed by its variant tag; a payload-carrying sum is keyed by its whole
encoded value, so `{ tag: "chunk", value: 4 }` and `{ tag: "chunk", value: 5 }`
are two different keys.

`direct` is the exception. It indexes exactly one column, and only `u8`, `u16`,
`u32`, `u64`, or a unit-variant enum.

```typescript
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"

const Kind = Stdb.enum("ping", "chunk")

const marker = Stdb.table("marker", {
  columns: {
    kind: Kind.index("btree"),
    seq: Stdb.u32(),
  },
  indexes: (columns) => [
    Stdb.index("byKindSeq", [columns.kind, columns.seq], {
      algorithm: "btree",
    }),
  ],
})

const Module = Stdb.Module.make("app").addTables(marker)
const { Db } = Module
```

## Composite Lookups

A composite btree index is read through the accessor named after the index. Pass
a tuple of index-column values: either a leading prefix of the columns or the
full width. The last value you supply may be a range; every column before it is
matched for equality.

```ts
const db = yield* Db

// Equality on both columns: a point lookup.
yield* db.marker.byKindSeq.filterToArray([{ tag: "chunk" }, 7])

// Equality on `kind`, range over `seq` — a range in the final column of a
// full-width tuple is a range scan, not a point lookup.
yield* db.marker.byKindSeq.filterToArray([
  { tag: "chunk" },
  { from: { tag: "included", value: 1 }, to: { tag: "excluded", value: 9 } },
])

// A one-column prefix scans every `seq` under that `kind`.
yield* db.marker.byKindSeq.filterToArray([{ tag: "chunk" }])
```

A single-column index takes the bare value or a bare `{ from, to }` range
instead of a tuple. Bounds are `{ tag: "included" | "excluded", value }` or
`{ tag: "unbounded" }`, and `delete(...)` accepts the same inputs as
`filterToArray(...)`.


---

# Source: /core-concepts/tables/performance

---
draft: false
title: Performance
description: Choose where table rows reside and understand the memory cost of indexes.
sidebar:
  order: 10
---

<a class="upstream-doc" href="https://spacetimedb.com/docs/tables/performance" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">SpacetimeDB: Performance ↗</a>

## Where rows reside

Set `cachePolicy` on a regular, scheduled, or outbox table. To set a default for the module, pass `settings: { tableCachePolicyDefault: "required_on_disk" }` to `Stdb.Module.make`. An explicit table policy takes precedence. Event tables never retain rows and cannot declare a policy.

```typescript
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"

const activeMatch = Stdb.table("activeMatch", {
  columns: { id: Stdb.u64().primaryKey() },
  cachePolicy: "required_in_memory",
})

const Module = Stdb.Module.make("matches", {
  settings: { tableCachePolicyDefault: "required_on_disk" },
}).addTables(activeMatch)
```

| Policy | Placement in SpacetimeDB 2.16 |
| --- | --- |
| `required_in_memory` | Keeps rows resident. This is the default. |
| `required_on_disk` | Allows the host to page cold data to local disk and keep hot data in memory. |
| `no_requirement` | Lets the host choose placement. Standalone treats it like `required_on_disk`. |

Indexes and system tables stay in memory. Both disk-capable policies require every index on the table to be a btree, including backing indexes for keys. Contract validation reports `CachePolicyRequiresBTree` with the table, index and source of the policy.

Standalone has an unlimited resident-memory budget. As of 2.16 the standard Maincloud limit is 24 GiB of resident memory per database. If a cold read fails or the host exceeds the budget, it ends execution and returns a failed internal outcome to the caller. A handler cannot catch that failure. Upstream plans to make `no_requirement` the default in 3.0. [SpacetimeDB tiered storage](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/tables/storage-and-cache-policies/)

Changing placement preserves rows during an [automatic migration](/core-concepts/databases/migrations). It leaves generated client bindings byte-identical.

## Subscribed client rows

The TypeScript SDK keeps subscribed rows in the client process regardless of their server placement. In 2.16.1 it also builds a tree for each subscribed btree index as rows arrive. Unique lookups and equality-prefix filters use these trees. A range on the first column still scans the cache. The SDK patch corrects range comparison for object-backed keys such as timestamps. Apply the patch in the consuming project when relying on those ranges. [Index syntax](/core-concepts/tables/indexes)


---

# Source: /core-concepts/tables/scheduled-tables

---
draft: false
title: Scheduled Tables
description: Use scheduled tables and scheduled reducers or procedures.
sidebar:
  order: 3
---

<a class="upstream-doc" href="https://spacetimedb.com/docs/tables/schedule-tables" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">SpacetimeDB: Scheduled Tables ↗</a>

Scheduled tables are private by default and reserve `scheduledId` and
`scheduledAt`. A scheduled endpoint receives `{ data: table.row }`.

`Stdb.scheduledTable(name, options)` auto-injects two columns before user
columns:

- `scheduledId`: a `u64().primaryKey().autoInc()` column with native column name
  `scheduled_id`.
- `scheduledAt`: a `ScheduleAt` column with native column name `scheduled_at`.

Authors cannot also declare `scheduledId`, `scheduledAt`, `scheduled_id`, or
`scheduled_at`; the constructor rejects those reserved names. A custom
`scheduledId` value type may be supplied through `options.scheduledId`, but it
must still be a `u64` value type and is still marked primary-key and auto-inc.

Scheduled tables default to `public: false`, the same local default as
`Stdb.table(...)`, and they honor an explicit `public: true`. User columns are
spread directly into the table shape after the injected scheduler columns; there
is no `{ data }` wrapper in the table row shape.

```typescript
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"

const reminderSchedule = Stdb.scheduledTable("reminderSchedule", {
  columns: {
    note: Stdb.string(),
  },
})

const Reminders = Stdb.Group.make("Reminders").add(
  Stdb.Fn.scheduledProcedure("reminderFire", {
    table: reminderSchedule,
  }),
)

const Module = Stdb.Module.make("app")
  .addTables(reminderSchedule)
  .add(Reminders)
const { Db } = Module

const RemindersLive = Stdb.Builder.group(Module, "Reminders", {
  reminderFire: Effect.fn(function* ({ data }) {
    yield* Effect.log(`reminder: ${data.note}`)
  }),
})
```

To seed schedule rows inside a reducer or transaction body, use the generated
`.schedule(...)` helper. It fills the auto-increment sentinel for you.

```ts
const db = yield* Db
yield* db.reminderSchedule.schedule({
  scheduledAt: Stdb.ScheduleAt.interval("5 minutes"),
  note: "wake up",
})
```

| Schedule form | Host behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Stdb.ScheduleAt.at(...)` or `after(...)` | One-shot row. Reducers consume it after execution; procedures consume it before, so a scheduled procedure can no longer find or update its own row. |
| `Stdb.ScheduleAt.interval(...)` | Row persists and re-fires until deleted. |

`Interval` covers plain re-fire spacing. Reach for self-rescheduling one-shot
rows when the target is a wall-clock or cron alignment an interval cannot
express: handle a `Time` row, insert the next one with
`Stdb.ScheduleAt.nextCron(cron, ctx.timestamp)` or `at(...)`, then return.

`Stdb.scheduledTable(...)` creates the reserved
`scheduled_id`/`scheduled_at` columns and `Fn.scheduledReducer(...)` or
`Fn.scheduledProcedure(...)` binds exactly one typed handler to the table.
The binding is registered on the function, which is where SpacetimeDB expects
it; the table itself carries no schedule option.

## Host Scheduling Semantics

These are SpacetimeDB host behaviours, not something this library adds.

**Dispatch is concurrent.** The scheduler does not wait for one due function to
finish before dispatching the next, so a slow scheduled procedure does not
delay unrelated scheduled work. Execution is bounded further down: scheduled
reducers share the module's single reducer lane and still run one at a time,
serialized with client-invoked reducers, while scheduled procedures take an
instance from a bounded pool — one per available CPU by default — and genuinely
run in parallel.

**Already-expired work has no order.** When several schedules are past due at
once, after a restart, a backlog, or an overrunning run, they are not guaranteed
to run in `scheduled_at` order. Never encode ordering between two schedule rows:
chain them, or carry an explicit sequence number in the row.

**A row does not normally overlap itself.** Each row is an independent schedule
identified by its `scheduledId`, and the host does not queue that row's next
invocation until the current one has returned. Two different rows in the same
table are separate schedules and may run at the same time. The exception is
re-arming: writing a schedule row registers its timer entry immediately, so a
procedure that updates its own row to an already-due time can be re-entered
while it is still running. Treat self-exclusion as the normal case, never as a
mutual-exclusion primitive.

**Intervals do not drift.** The next fire time is the previous *intended* time
plus the interval, not the time the last run started or finished, so timer
jitter and slow runs never accumulate. Ticks missed while the database was busy
or down are skipped rather than replayed back to back. The first fire of a newly
inserted `Interval` row is one interval away, not immediate.

**A scheduled reducer is still one transaction.** Its whole body commits or
rolls back atomically, exactly like a client-invoked reducer. For a one-shot
row, the host's deletion of that row is a separate transaction committed
immediately afterwards — subscribers see two updates — and it happens whether
the reducer succeeded or failed. Failed invocations are logged and never
retried; re-insert a schedule row from the handler if retry is part of the
domain.

## Scheduled Procedures Must Claim Their Work

A procedure has no ambient transaction: each `Tx.run(...)` is its own
transaction, and external work such as an HTTP call necessarily happens between
two of them. The host holds nothing across that gap — no row locks, no snapshot,
no exclusion. Combined with concurrent dispatch, a procedure that selects
pending rows in one transaction, calls out, and marks them done in a later
transaction will hand the same rows to a second invocation that starts in the
window between the two.

Claim the work in the same transaction that selects it: flip a status column, or
stamp an attempt id and a lease expiry, so the selecting transaction is what
makes those rows invisible to everyone else. Do the external call afterwards and
record its outcome against that claim.

Keep transaction bodies idempotent and free of captured mutable state for the
same reason procedures generally require it: the runtime may re-run a
transaction body after a commit conflict.

## Validation Boundaries

The TypeScript DSL rejects raw schemas in SATS positions at compile time by
requiring opaque value types. Cross-object module invariants are validated by
`validateModule` / `Stdb.validate`:

| Invariant | Compile-time | Runtime validation diagnostic |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Raw Effect schema in a SATS position | Yes | `UnsupportedTypeDescriptor` remains as a malformed-spec fallback |
| Duplicate table/view relation names | No | `DuplicateRelationName` |
| Duplicate reducer/procedure/HTTP/view/lifecycle export names | No | `DuplicateCallableName` |
| Reserved `__http_router__` export name | No | `DuplicateCallableName` |
| Declared names without a representable generated accessor | No | `NonCanonicalDeclaredName` |
| Reserved declared error tags | No | `ReservedDeclaredErrorTag` |
| Duplicate declared error tags | No | `DuplicateDeclaredErrorTag` |
| String literal authored/generated-client tag collisions | No | `LiteralTagCollision` |

Broad cross-group uniqueness checks stay in runtime validation because lifting
large cross-object comparisons into the type system can hit TypeScript
instantiation-depth limits. Smaller bounded checks, such as reserved names and
casing policy, are better candidates for future compile-time feedback.


---

# Source: /core-concepts/testing

---
draft: false
title: Testing
description: Run a module's handlers in-process with the test harness, bindCallables and the inter-database pump.
sidebar:
  order: 8
---

`effect-spacetimedb/testing` runs a module without a server. The harness is an
in-memory database behind the real Effect DB wrapper, and `bindCallables` calls
your handlers the way the host does, so a test exercises the handlers you
publish. For what only a real host can show, publish to a local server: see
[Dev & Publish](/core-concepts/databases/dev-publish).

## Vitest configuration

```ts title="vitest.config.ts"
import { spacetimeSysAlias } from "effect-spacetimedb/testing"
import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config"

export default defineConfig({
  resolve: { alias: { ...spacetimeSysAlias } },
  test: {
    server: { deps: { inline: ["spacetimedb", "effect-spacetimedb"] } },
  },
})
```

`spacetimeSysAlias` points the host syscalls at a stub, and `inline` makes Vitest
transform both packages so the alias reaches their imports. Without
`effect-spacetimedb` in that list, Node loads it untransformed and fails with
`Only URLs with a scheme in: file, data, and node are supported... Received
protocol 'spacetime:'`.

The stub keeps `console` and the deterministic backstops usable off-host, so
importing or building a module entry in a test needs no running host.

## Calling a handler

`makeTestModuleHarness` takes the module's spec and owns one database.
`bindCallables` takes the module and the same implementations you pass to
`build`, which is why they live in a file of their own: a module entry may export
nothing but its compiled output. Continuing the module from
[Getting Started](/getting-started):

```ts title="test/messages.test.ts"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import { bindCallables, makeTestModuleHarness } from "effect-spacetimedb/testing"
import { expect, it } from "vitest"
import { QuickstartModule } from "../src/contract.ts"
import { MessageFunctionsLive } from "../src/live.ts"

const callables = bindCallables(QuickstartModule, [MessageFunctionsLive])

it("stores a message", async () => {
  const harness = makeTestModuleHarness(QuickstartModule.spec, { seed: 1n })
  const id = "ada"

  callables.messageSend?.invoke(harness.makeMutationCtx(), { id, text: "Hello" })

  const rows = await Effect.runPromise(harness.effectDb.message.toArray())
  expect(rows).toEqual([{ id, text: "Hello" }])
})
```

`bindCallables` returns a record keyed by function name, of `invoke(ctx, args)`
functions that run in a harness transaction. It is loosely typed: with
`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` a member may be `undefined`, and `args` is not checked
against the contract. The context comes from the harness, one maker per kind of
function:

| Function | Context |
| --- | --- |
| reducer, lifecycle hook | `harness.makeMutationCtx()` |
| procedure | `harness.makeProcedureCtx()` |
| HTTP handler | `harness.makeHttpHandlerCtx()` |
| sender view | `harness.makeViewCtx()` |
| anonymous view | `harness.makeAnonymousViewCtx()` |

Each takes overrides, such as `{ sender }` or `{ timestamp }`.

### What a call answers

A reducer returns nothing, and throws as the host would: a declared error throws
a `SenderError`, and any other failure throws its cause. Its transaction rolls
back either way.

`invoke` hands `args` to the handler as they are, and returns a procedure's result
without encoding it. So a test cannot reach what a host does around the handler:
a bad argument's `SenderError` or `BadArguments` reply, or a result that fails to
encode. Prove those on a real host.

A procedure never throws. It answers with `{ ok: value }` or `{ err: string }`,
where `err` is the encoded declared error or a fixed message. A test of an
undeclared failure therefore reads the cause through `onDefect`, which fires once
per failure as it does in `build`:

```ts title="test/message-list.test.ts"
import type * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import { bindCallables, makeTestModuleHarness } from "effect-spacetimedb/testing"
import { expect, it } from "vitest"
import { QuickstartModule } from "../src/contract.ts"
import { MessageFunctionsLive } from "../src/live.ts"

it("answers with the rows", () => {
  const causes: Array<Cause.Cause<unknown>> = []
  const callables = bindCallables(QuickstartModule, [MessageFunctionsLive], {
    onDefect: (cause) => causes.push(cause),
  })
  const harness = makeTestModuleHarness(QuickstartModule.spec, { seed: 1n })

  const reply = callables.messageList?.invoke(harness.makeProcedureCtx(), {})

  expect(reply).toEqual({ ok: [] })
  expect(causes).toEqual([])
})
```

## Reading and resetting

`harness.effectDb` is the module's typed database, the same `db` a handler gets,
and its reads are Effects. `harness.db` is the raw store, which takes and returns
native host column values.

Transactions snapshot the store, roll back while preserving row identity, and
reject nesting with `NestedTestTransactionDefect`. A rollback restores rows but
not sequences, the uuid counter or the random stream. `harness.reset()` empties
every table and restarts all three, for a suite that wants a fresh database per
test without building a new harness. The `seed` option is a `bigint` and fixes
the random stream; scheduled rows are stored without emulating the scheduler.

A module that declares an environment takes its values as a publish does; see
[Environment Variables](/core-concepts/databases/environment-variables#testing).
A rejected environment throws `TestModuleEnvironmentDefect`.

## Mounted modules

Give `makeTestModuleHarness` the parent spec and pass the parent module and its implementation tuple to `bindCallables`. Invoke a mounted callable by its nested accessor or its full canonical wire name. Inspect rows through `harness.db.<mount>.<table>`. Root and library writes share the transaction, including rollback.

For a native mount used by the test, supply `nativeMounts` in the harness options. For example, `{ nativeMounts: { "stockRoom.tools": parent => makeToolsAlias(parent) } }` builds a stand-in for that path on first access in a context. Its return value is the object passed to the native helper. An absent factory raises an error identifying the path when accessed. See [Submodules](/core-concepts/databases/submodules).

## Inter-database calls

`makeIdcPump` delivers outbox rows between harnesses in memory, one stream at a
time, and takes `IdcPump.recording(...)` for a receiver the test does not
simulate. `pump.drain()` delivers until nothing waits, at most 1,000 times unless
`deliveriesMax` says otherwise, and throws a `RangeError` if rows still wait at
that bound. See
[Inter-Database Calls](/core-concepts/functions/inter-database-calls).

## What is exported

| Name | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `makeTestModuleHarness` | The in-memory database. Types: `TestModuleHarness`, `TestModuleRawDb`, `TestModuleRowWrite`, `OutboxTableKeys`, `TestModuleEnvironmentValues`, `TestModuleEnvironmentUpdate`. Errors: `TestModuleEnvironmentDefect`, `NestedTestTransactionDefect`. |
| `bindCallables` | Call handlers. |
| `makeIdcPump`, `IdcPump`, `IdcDelivery` | Deliver inter-database calls in memory. Types: `IdcPumpDatabase`, `IdcPumpLink`, `IdcPumpReceiver`, `IdcPumpRecordingReceiver`, `IdcRecordedCall`. |
| `Expand` | The helper type a harness's module type prints with, so a test helper's declarations can name it. |
| `spacetimeSysAlias` | The alias map above. |
| `SpacetimeSysStub` | The stub as a namespace, for backing `env_get` with `withEnvironment`. |

`effect-spacetimedb/testing/spacetime-sys` is the stub itself, for a bundler or
test runner that takes a path rather than an alias map.


---

# Source: /getting-started

---
draft: false
title: Getting Started
description: From an empty directory to a reducer call on a local SpacetimeDB, with effect-spacetimedb.
sidebar:
  order: 1
---

import { TabItem, Tabs } from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

`effect-spacetimedb` is an Effect-first authoring layer for SpaceTimeDB modules.
You describe the module once, implement handlers with scoped Effect services,
then build native module exports and clients from the same contract.

This page goes from an empty directory to a reducer call on a server running on
your machine. The commands use Bun, which runs TypeScript directly; the install
step shows npm and pnpm too. Node.js must satisfy `^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1`.

## Install the CLI

```sh
curl -sSf https://install.spacetimedb.com | sh
spacetime version install 2.16.1 --use
spacetime --version
```

Open a new terminal if `spacetime` is not found yet: the installer adds it to
your `PATH`. `spacetime --version` must report `2.16.1`. The CLI version must match the
`spacetimedb` package your project depends on, because `spacetime build` and
`spacetime generate` read a version-specific module format. If several versions
are installed, make sure the matching `spacetime` is the one on your `PATH`.

## Start a local server

In a terminal of its own:

```sh
spacetime start
```

It listens on port 3000 and keeps running. A fresh CLI's default server is
Maincloud, the hosted service, so the commands below all say `--server local`.

## Create the project

```sh
mkdir stdb-hello
cd stdb-hello
echo '{ "name": "stdb-hello", "private": true, "type": "module" }' > package.json
```

<Tabs syncKey="package-manager">
  <TabItem label="bun">

    ```sh
    bun add effect-spacetimedb effect@4.1.1 spacetimedb@2.16.1
    bun add --dev typescript @types/node
    ```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="npm">

    ```sh
    npm install effect-spacetimedb effect@4.1.1 spacetimedb@2.16.1
    npm install --save-dev typescript @types/node
    ```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="pnpm">

    ```sh
    pnpm add effect-spacetimedb effect@4.1.1 spacetimedb@2.16.1
    pnpm add --save-dev typescript @types/node
    ```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

Add a `tsconfig.json`. `moduleResolution` must be `Bundler`: under `nodenext`
the code `spacetime generate` writes fails with `TS2305`.

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "strict": true,
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "types": ["node"]
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*.ts"]
}
```

## Write the module

A module is three files, split for a reason: a client must not import the module
entry. The entry loads the host-only `spacetime:sys` modules, which exist only
inside the server, so importing it elsewhere fails with
`Cannot find package 'spacetime:sys@2.2'` on Bun and
`ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME` on Node.

The contract declares the table and the callable functions. Everything else
imports it, and it imports nothing host-only.

```ts title="src/contract.ts"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"

export const message = Stdb.table("message", {
  public: true,
  columns: {
    id: Stdb.string().primaryKey(),
    text: Stdb.string(),
  },
})

export const MessageRow = Stdb.struct({
  id: Stdb.string(),
  text: Stdb.string(),
}).named("MessageRow")

export const MessageFunctions = Stdb.Group.make("Messages").add(
  Stdb.Fn.reducer("messageSend", {
    params: MessageRow,
  }),
  Stdb.Fn.procedure("messageList", {
    params: Stdb.struct({}),
    returns: Stdb.array(MessageRow),
  }),
)

export const QuickstartModule = Stdb.Module.make(
  "effect_spacetimedb_quickstart",
  {},
)
  .addTables(message)
  .add(MessageFunctions)
```

The implementation attaches a handler to each function. Handlers get what they
need by yielding services from the module.

```ts title="src/live.ts"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"
import { QuickstartModule } from "./contract.ts"

const { Db, Tx } = QuickstartModule

export const MessageFunctionsLive = Stdb.Builder.group(
  QuickstartModule,
  "Messages",
  {
    messageSend: Effect.fn(function* ({ id, text }) {
      const db = yield* Db
      yield* db.message.insert({ id, text })
    }),
    messageList: Effect.fn(function* () {
      const tx = yield* Tx
      return yield* tx.run(
        Effect.gen(function* () {
          const db = yield* Db
          return yield* db.message.toArray()
        }),
      )
    }),
  },
)
```

The entry compiles the module. Its only exports are `ModuleExports` and the
default schema: the SDK rejects any other named export, including an
`export *` of the contract, with `TypeError: exporting something that is not a
spacetime export`. A type-only re-export is erased and safe.

```ts title="src/index.ts"
import { build } from "effect-spacetimedb/server-compiler"
import { QuickstartModule } from "./contract.ts"
import { MessageFunctionsLive } from "./live.ts"

export type { QuickstartClientExample } from "./client.ts"

const compiled = build(QuickstartModule, [MessageFunctionsLive])

export const ModuleExports = compiled.exportGroup()

export default compiled.schema
```

A contract that declares Effect `HttpApi` routes, or anything else that loads
Effect's HTTP or encoding modules before `server-compiler` is imported, needs
`import "effect-spacetimedb/server-polyfills"` as the entry's first line.

## Publish it

From the project directory, build the module and publish it to the local server
under the database name `stdb-hello`. Database names are lowercase words joined
by dashes.

```sh
spacetime publish --server local --yes stdb-hello
```

## Call a reducer

The client imports only the contract. `Stdb.project` turns it into a typed
client with no generated code.

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"
import type * as StdbClient from "effect-spacetimedb/client"
import { QuickstartModule } from "./contract.ts"

const Quickstart = Stdb.project(QuickstartModule.spec)

/** Typechecked client calls shown in the package quick start. */
const clientExample = (
  http: StdbClient.ProjectedHttpClient<typeof QuickstartModule.spec>,
  session: StdbClient.WsSession<typeof QuickstartModule.spec>,
  messageId: string,
) => ({
  call: http.procedures.messageList({}),
  subscribe: session.subscribe(
    Quickstart.targets.tables.message.where((row) => row.id.eq(messageId)),
  ),
})

export type QuickstartClientExample = ReturnType<typeof clientExample>
```

Use a separate entry to run an HTTP call against the local database.

```ts title="src/send.ts"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as FetchHttpClient from "effect/http/FetchHttpClient"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"
import { QuickstartModule } from "./contract.ts"

const client = Stdb.project(QuickstartModule.spec).client.http.make({
  uri: "http://127.0.0.1:3000",
  databaseName: "stdb-hello",
})

const program = Effect.gen(function* () {
  yield* client.reducers.messageSend({ id: "first", text: "Hello" })
  yield* Effect.log(yield* client.procedures.messageList({}))
})

Effect.runPromise(program.pipe(Effect.provide(FetchHttpClient.layer)))
```

```sh
bun run src/send.ts
```

It logs the row it wrote. Typecheck the project with:

```sh
bunx tsc
```

The optional `token` in the client's config is a SpacetimeDB identity token.
Without one, the server treats each call as a new anonymous identity.

## Develop

`spacetime dev` rebuilds and republishes on every change, and keeps generated
client bindings in `src/module_bindings` up to date:

```sh
spacetime dev --server local --module-path . --server-only --yes stdb-hello
```

Run `spacetime generate` by hand for bindings without a dev loop. A WebSocket
session and its live subscriptions take them as its `DbConnection`; see
[Connection](/core-concepts/clients/connection).

```sh
spacetime generate --lang typescript --module-path . --out-dir src/module_bindings --yes
```

:::note

Plain `spacetime generate` is the default and its `DbConnection` can be passed
directly to the Effect client. Projects that do not want generated TypeScript in
their stricter type graph can use the published quarantined artifact pipeline
and a spec-typed facade described in [Codegen](/core-concepts/clients/codegen).

:::

## Patch the SDK

The patch fixes [client range comparisons for object-backed keys](https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5970),
[host index classification for overlapping constraints](https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5969)
and [branded primitive inputs to native builders](https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6660)
in SDK 2.16.1.

Before relying on these SDK features, copy
[`patches/spacetimedb@2.16.1.patch`](https://github.com/miragegame/effect-spacetimedb/blob/v0.9.0/patches/spacetimedb@2.16.1.patch)
into your project. Its paths are relative to the `spacetimedb` package root, so
Bun applies it from your root `package.json`, and pnpm from the same entry
under `pnpm.patchedDependencies` or in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

```json
{
  "patchedDependencies": {
    "spacetimedb@2.16.1": "patches/spacetimedb@2.16.1.patch"
  }
}
```

Other package managers need their own patch mechanism. Apply it wherever the
SDK is installed, module and client packages alike.

## The same module in the native SDK

For comparison, the table and reducer above with no Effect layer. The params
accept any string, and the failure paths are yours to write.

```ts
import { schema, table, t } from "spacetimedb/server"

const spacetime = schema({
  message: table(
    { public: true },
    { id: t.string().primaryKey(), text: t.string() },
  ),
})

// The exported binding's name is the reducer name.
export const message_send = spacetime.reducer(
  { id: t.string(), text: t.string() },
  (ctx, { id, text }) => {
    ctx.db.message.insert({ id, text })
  },
)

export default spacetime
```

# Source: /reference

---
draft: false
title: Reference
description: Entrypoints, capability scopes, value-type helpers, and declared-error rules.
sidebar:
  order: 99
---

This is a curated reference for the public surface. It is intentionally
hand-written; there is no generated API reference.

## Entrypoints

| Entrypoint | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `effect-spacetimedb` | Contract builders, value types, tables, declared errors, module assembly, builder APIs, and client projection. |
| `effect-spacetimedb/client` | WebSocket generated-client adapters and client transport helpers. |
| `effect-spacetimedb/client/atom` | Effect Atom bindings for React consumers; needs the optional `@effect/atom-react` and `react` peers. |
| `effect-spacetimedb/codegen` | Quarantined generation: runs the native generator and emits an erased client artifact (`generateArtifact`) or receiver binding (`generateReceiverArtifact`), each with a drift check. |
| `effect-spacetimedb/server` | Advanced server primitives for integrations that bypass normal builder flow. |
| `effect-spacetimedb/server-compiler` | Host-only compiler entrypoint for module entries; import `build` from here. |
| `effect-spacetimedb/server-polyfills` | Side-effect import for host compatibility shims; normal module entries get these through `server-compiler`, and an entry that loads Effect's HTTP or encoding modules first imports it first. |
| `effect-spacetimedb/dev-server` | Programmatic local `spacetimedb-standalone` orchestration for tests and tools that publish prebuilt bundles, one database or several on one standalone. |
| `effect-spacetimedb/testing` | The off-host test harness: `makeTestModuleHarness`, `bindCallables`, `makeIdcPump`, and the `spacetimeSysAlias` map for tests that import a module entry. See [Testing](/core-concepts/testing). |
| `effect-spacetimedb/testing/spacetime-sys` | Direct `spacetime:sys` host-surface stub for off-host module imports. |

Normal module authors usually need only `effect-spacetimedb` and, for WebSocket
sessions, `effect-spacetimedb/client`.

## Client constructors

| Entry | Constructors |
| --- | --- |
| `/client` over HTTP | `httpMake` |
| `/client` over WebSocket | `wsMake`, `wsScoped`, `wsScopedGenerated`, `wsLayer`, `wsLayerGenerated`, `wsSupervisor`, `wsSupervisorGenerated` |
| WebSocket integration | `wsGeneratedConnection` types a generated connection class. `wsSessionTag` creates a session service tag. `wsConnectAndSubscribe` acquires a session and subscribes before returning it. |
| `/client/atom` | `wsSupervisedSessionAtom`, `wsTableAtomFamily`, `wsRowAtomFamily`, `wsTableGroupAtomFamily`, `wsTableGroupSnapshotAtom` |

## Capability Scoping

| Scope | Allowed accessors |
| --- | --- |
| reducer, lifecycle | `Db`, `ReducerCtx`, `MutationCtx` |
| procedure outside a transaction | platform `Http`, `Tx`, `ProcedureCtx` |
| `Tx.run(...)` body | `Db`, `MutationCtx`, transaction context |
| `HttpTx.run(...)` body | `Db` |
| HTTP handler | `HttpTx`, `HttpHandlerCtx` |
| sender view | `ReadonlyDb`, `From`, `ViewCtx` |
| anonymous view | `ReadonlyDb`, `From`, `AnonymousViewCtx` |
| every scope above, once the module declares an environment | `Env` |

Use `MutationCtx` for helpers that must run in both reducers and procedure
transaction bodies; an HTTP handler has no sender, so `MutationCtx` in an
`HttpTx.run` body is a compile error. Do not yield accessors from another module.

## Value-Type Cheat Sheet

| Helper | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Stdb.string(schema?)` | SATS string with optional Effect schema branding or checks. |
| `Stdb.u8` / `u16` / `u32` / `u64` | Unsigned integer widths with constructor-owned bounds. |
| `Stdb.u128` / `u256` | Wide unsigned integer widths backed by `bigint`. |
| `Stdb.i8` / `i16` / `i32` / `i64` | Signed integer widths. |
| `Stdb.i128` / `i256` | Wide signed integer widths backed by `bigint`. |
| `Stdb.f32()` / `f64()` | Floating-point value types. |
| `Stdb.bigint()` | `bigint` authored value lowered to a SATS string for JSON-safe large numbers. |
| `Stdb.bool()` | Boolean value. |
| `Stdb.bytes()` | `Uint8Array` byte array. |
| `Stdb.identity()` / `connectionId()` | Native SpacetimeDB identity and connection id values. |
| `Stdb.timestamp()` / `timeDuration()` / `uuid()` | Native timestamp, duration, and UUID values. |
| `Stdb.scheduleAt()` | Scheduled-table `scheduledAt` column value type. |
| `Stdb.option(T)` | Nullable value type, decoded as `T` or `undefined`. |
| `Stdb.optional(T)` | Optional struct field annotation. |
| `T.optional()` | Optional table column annotation. |
| `Stdb.array(T)` / `Stdb.array(T, { minimum, maximum })` | SATS array/list. Either inclusive length bound is optional; a bound is enforced by the codecs, not on the wire. |
| `Stdb.struct({...})` | Named object shape for params, rows, returns, and errors. |
| `Stdb.sum({...})` | Tagged union with payload variants; key- and index-capable, never auto-increment. |
| `T.named("Name")` | Set the generated SATS/client type name for an anonymous struct, sum, or string-literal enum; the default name is content-addressed. |
| `Stdb.enum("a", "b")` | Unit-variant SATS enum; needs the namespace form because `enum` cannot be named-imported. |
| `Stdb.unit()` | Unit value for empty scheduled procedure returns, result branches, and sum payloads. |
| `Stdb.literal(...)` | String, number, or boolean literal values; string literals lower to enums. |
| `Stdb.result(Ok, Err)` | Result envelope value type. |
| `Stdb.dbCodec(T)` / `httpCodec(T)` / `wsCodec(T)` | Transport codecs for DB/host, HTTP JSON, and generated WebSocket client shapes. |
| `Stdb.lazy(() => T)` | Recursive value type reference. |
| `Stdb.custom(schema, { type })` | Custom schema with explicit SpaceTimeDB type lowering. |

See [Value Types](/the-effect-layer/value-types) for the canonical catalog with
TypeScript values, SATS lowering, bounds, and transport encoding notes.

## Authoring API

| Surface | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `Stdb.table(...)` / `scheduledTable(...)` | Declare persistent, event, and scheduled tables. |
| `Stdb.index(...)` / `unique(...)` | Declare table indexes and uniqueness constraints. |
| `Stdb.Fn.reducer(...)` / `procedure(...)` / `scheduledReducer(...)` / `scheduledProcedure(...)` / `view(...)` / `anonymousView(...)` | Declare callable and view endpoints. |
| `Stdb.Group.make(...)` / `Stdb.HttpGroup.make(...)` | Group reducers/procedures/views and HTTP routes. |
| `Stdb.Http.*` | Declare typed and raw HTTP handlers. |
| `Stdb.Module.make(...)` | Assemble tables, callable groups, HTTP groups, lifecycle, and settings. |
| `Module.mount(key, child, options?)` / `Module.mountNative<Library>()(key, options?)` | Declare a namespace. Set `options.name` to pin its canonical name. |
| `Stdb.Builder.mount(...)` / `mountNative(...)` | Supply a child and its implementations or a native SDK namespace in the parent's build. |
| `Module.mounts[key].run(effect)` / `.use(fn)` / `.use(kind, fn)` | Run an Effect in the child scope or invoke a native helper with its alias. Direct Effect table handles nest under `Db` and `ReadonlyDb`. See [Submodules](/core-concepts/databases/submodules). |
| `Stdb.Builder.group(...)` / `groupPrechecked(...)` / `lifecycle(...)` | Attach Effect implementations to an assembled module. |
| `Stdb.project(Module)` | Build client projections, targets, and generated-client adapters. |
| `Stdb.toHttpApi(Module)` / `httpApiBaseUrl(...)` | Project typed HTTP routes into Effect `HttpApi`. |
| `Stdb.ScheduleAt.*` | Build scheduled table `scheduledAt` values. |
| `Stdb.Environment.*` | Declare typed database environment keys for `Module.make(id, { environment })`. |
| `Stdb.validate(...)` / `assertValid(...)` / `formatModuleDiagnostics(...)` | Run module validation manually. |

Builder impl values are sealed. `GroupImpl<Name, RuntimeR, ModuleName>` and
`LifecycleImpl<Hooks, RuntimeR, ModuleName>` expose only build-time group,
lifecycle, runtime-requirement, and module-identity phantoms; handler
definitions are private to the builder pipeline. The module-name parameter
defaults to `string` so older two-argument annotations still compile, but
`build(...)` rejects widened impl annotations. Keep
implementation arrays inferred with `as const` when storing them before
`build(...)`.

`groupPrechecked(...)` returns `GroupImpl<Name, never>` for handler records that
already satisfy `GroupCheckedHandlers<Module, Name>`. That annotation allows only
the server-context services valid for each endpoint kind and the current module's
accessors. Cross-module accessors are rejected through the Effect requirements
channel; the legacy `effect-spacetimedb/server` section/single-handler
validators remain module-blind for compatibility, while transaction helpers keep
branded residual runner requirements for transaction-family coherence. Use
`group(...)` when a handler intentionally requires a custom service and provide a
runtime to `build(...)`.

## Declared Error Catalog

Declared errors are created with a namespace:

```ts
const AppErrors = Stdb.errors.namespace("App")({
  UserMissing: Stdb.error({ userId: Stdb.string(UserId) }, { status: 404 }),
})
```

The catalog value supplies:

| Surface | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| generated classes | Fail directly from handlers with typed payloads. |
| `.schema` | Decode and encode the declared error envelope. |
| `.tags` | Known wire tags for client and route projection. |
| `.pick(...)` | Narrow a catalog to selected declared errors. |

:::caution

Only Effect failures are encoded as declared errors. Defects remain defects.

:::

## Runtime And Client Error Types

| Type | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `HandlerAsyncNotAllowedDefect` | Async, promises, timers, microtasks, or `Effect.sleep` in synchronous server handlers. |
| `HandlerGlobalRandomNotAllowedDefect` | Global `Math.random` use in guarded server runtime. |
| `HandlerWallClockNotAllowedDefect` | Ambient `Date.now()` or no-argument `new Date()` in guarded server runtime. |
| `StdbTableOperationDefect` | A server table invariant failed. Inspect `table`, `op` and `cause`. |
| `StdbHostCallError` | Generic host ABI call failure. |
| `StdbUniqueAlreadyExistsError` / `StdbNoSuchRowError` / `StdbAutoIncOverflowError` / `StdbScheduleDelayTooLongError` | Typed native host failures. |
| `StdbDecodeError` | Contract decode failure. |
| `CallFailure<E>` / `RawCallFailure<E>` | Projected HTTP call failure unions. |
| `WsCallFailure<E>` / `RawWsCallFailure<E>` / `WsConnectionFailure` | Projected WebSocket call failure unions, and what a session adds: `ConnectionLostError`, `CallNotSentError`, `ConnectionIdentityChangedError`. |
| `RemoteRejectedError` / `TransportError` / `DomainCallError<E>` | Projected client remote, transport, and raw declared-error failures. A `TransportError` whose `cause` is `HttpCallDurationExceededError` overran `callDurationMax`. |
| `WsConnectError` / `WsConnectTimeoutError` | WebSocket acquisition failed, or did not complete in time. |
| `ConnectionLostError` | An established connection was lost while the call was in flight, or the session had ended; the call's outcome is unknown. |
| `CallNotSentError` | Automatic reconnect: the call was refused unsent while the session reconnected. |
| `ConnectionIdentityChangedError` | Automatic reconnect: a reconnect changed the identity and ended the session. |
| `GeneratedArtifactShapeError` | The generated client is missing relations the contract declares. |

# Source: /the-effect-layer/migrating-from-native-sdk

---
draft: false
title: Migrating From Native SDK Shape
description: Move from native SpaceTimeDB module code to effect-spacetimedb contracts incrementally.
sidebar:
  order: 8
---

import { TabItem, Tabs } from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

:::tip

You do not need to rewrite a whole module at once. Start by modeling the module
contract, then move handlers behind the typed builder group by group.

:::

For an existing effect-spacetimedb 0.8 application, follow [Upgrading from 0.8 to 0.9](/the-effect-layer/upgrading-from-0-8).

## The Same Module, Both Ways

The native module and the equivalent effect-spacetimedb contract — declare the
shape, then implement handlers behind the typed group:

<Tabs syncKey="impl">
  <TabItem label="Native SDK">

```ts
import { schema, table, t } from "spacetimedb/server"

const spacetime = schema({
  user: table(
    { public: true },
    { id: t.string().primaryKey(), name: t.string() },
  ),
})

export const user_upsert = spacetime.reducer(
  { id: t.string(), name: t.string() },
  (ctx, { id, name }) => {
    ctx.db.user.insert({ id, name })
  },
)

export default spacetime
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="effect-spacetimedb">

```ts
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"

// 1. declare the contract
const user = Stdb.table("user", {
  public: true,
  columns: {
    id: Stdb.string().primaryKey(),
    name: Stdb.string(),
  },
})

const Users = Stdb.Group.make("Users").add(
  Stdb.Fn.reducer("userUpsert", {
    params: Stdb.struct({ id: Stdb.string(), name: Stdb.string() }),
  }),
)

const Module = Stdb.Module.make("app").addTables(user).add(Users)
const { Db } = Module

// 2. implement handlers behind the typed group
const UsersLive = Stdb.Builder.group(Module, "Users", {
  userUpsert: (args) =>
    Effect.gen(function* () {
      const db = yield* Db
      yield* db.user.insert(args)
    }),
})
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Native Shape To Contract Shape

| Native concept | effect-spacetimedb concept |
| --- | --- |
| reducer function export | `Fn.reducer(...)` in a callable group |
| procedure function export | `Fn.procedure(...)` in a callable group |
| `table({ cachePolicy }, columns)` | Pass the same literal to `Stdb.table`, `Stdb.scheduledTable`, or `Stdb.outboxTable`. Set a module-wide fallback with `settings.tableCachePolicyDefault`. |
| table builder | `Stdb.table(...)` bound to a variable |
| `reducer`/`procedure` `onSchedule` option | `Fn.scheduledReducer(...)` or `scheduledProcedure(...)` |
| `schema({ ns: lib })` | Declare `.mount("ns", Library)` for an Effect contract, or `.mountNative<typeof import("lib")>()("ns")` for a native library. Implement the declaration in the parent build. |
| `ctx.db.ns` | Use the Effect child table handles at `(yield* Parent.Db).ns`, or the corresponding readonly handles in a root view. |
| `ctx.as.ns` | Use `Parent.mounts.ns.use(fn)` for a native mutation helper, or select the procedure or HTTP kind. Run an Effect library operation with `Parent.mounts.ns.run(effect)`. See [Submodules](/core-concepts/databases/submodules). |
| HTTP handler export | `HttpGroup` plus `Builder.group(...)` |

Schedules are registered on the function, not the table: `Fn.scheduledReducer(...)`
and `scheduledProcedure(...)` compile to the native `onSchedule` option, which is
where SpacetimeDB now expects the binding. If you are porting a module that
passes `scheduled` to `table(...)`, that registration is deprecated upstream —
drop it and declare the scheduled callable instead.

## Suggested Order

1. Move schemas and table declarations into leaf files.
2. Declare groups without changing runtime behavior.
3. Assemble a module and destructure the typed accessors.
4. Port handlers one group at a time.
5. Generate the client and replace ad hoc call sites with projected clients.

Keep the runtime constraints in mind: module handlers must remain synchronous,
deterministic, and transactional. Network calls, timers, and secrets belong
outside reducers and are passed in as arguments or handled by external services.


---

# Source: /the-effect-layer/option-vs-optional

---
draft: false
title: Stdb.option vs Stdb.optional
description: Choose value nullability or field optionality intentionally.
sidebar:
  order: 6
---

`Stdb.option(T)` is a nullable value type. Its decoded TypeScript value is
`T | undefined`, and its SATS wire type is `option<T>`. Use it anywhere a value
type is allowed: arguments, array elements, table columns, nested types, and
struct fields. In a struct field, the key is still required.

`Stdb.optional(T)` and `.optional()` are field or column optionality annotations.
They mean the struct field or table column itself may be omitted. In struct and
callable param fields they lower to the same SATS `option<T>` wire type as
`Stdb.option(T)`.

Rule of thumb:

- Use `Stdb.option` for standalone nullable values and fields that are always
  present but may be none.
- Use `Stdb.optional` or `.optional()` when the property or column may be
  omitted.

The wire shape is the same for struct fields; the TypeScript shape differs:
`Stdb.optional(T)` gives `x?: T`, while `Stdb.option(T)` gives
`x: T | undefined`.


---

# Source: /the-effect-layer/randomness-and-determinism

---
draft: false
title: Randomness And Determinism
description: Deterministic randomness for reducers, and why it is not secret.
sidebar:
  order: 5
---

Reducers must be deterministic. Every replica needs to reproduce the same result
from the same logged inputs. Use the timestamp supplied by the host and the
SDK’s deterministic random stream.

## Reducer Randomness

Inside Effect-based reducers, use `Random.*` from `effect/Random`. The constrained server
runtime wires Effect randomness to the call context's deterministic random
stream.

```typescript
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Random from "effect/Random"

const roll = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const die = yield* Random.nextIntBetween(1, 6)
  const fraction = yield* Random.next
  return { die, fraction }
})
```

:::caution

Do not call global `Math.random` in reducers, procedures, views, or HTTP handler
effects. Development guards replace it with a throwing stub so accidental use
fails early.

:::

## Wall Clock

Use the call timestamp supplied by the current context instead of ambient clock
globals. In guarded development runs, `Date.now()` and no-argument `new Date()`
throw `HandlerWallClockNotAllowedDefect`; `Math.random` throws
`HandlerGlobalRandomNotAllowedDefect`; suspended Effects, promises, timers, and
microtasks throw `HandlerAsyncNotAllowedDefect`.

The Effect clock is wired to the same transaction timestamp, so `Effect.Clock`
and `DateTime.now` are deterministic inside server handlers.

## UUID Helpers

Reducer, transaction, and HTTP handler contexts expose deterministic UUID
helpers. Use `ctx.newUuidV4()` and `ctx.newUuidV7()` when a row needs a stable
identifier produced inside server module code.

```typescript
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"

const { ReducerCtx } = Module

const ids = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const ctx = yield* ReducerCtx
  return {
    randomId: ctx.newUuidV4(),
    timeSortableId: ctx.newUuidV7(),
  }
})
```

:::caution

The SDK seeds each call’s random stream from its timestamp alone and restarts
the UUID v7 counter for each call. In 2.16.1 four PCG32 outputs expand that
64-bit seed to fill the whole 128-bit generator state. Two transactions given
the same timestamp still draw the same sequence and can mint duplicate UUIDs.
For unique keys, mint IDs from a sequence advanced inside the transaction.

:::

## Runtime Wiring

The constrained server runtime wires `Random.*` from `effect/Random` to the
current SpaceTimeDB call context through `ctx.random`, so helpers such as
`Random.next`, `Random.nextIntBetween`, and `Random.shuffle` consume the same
deterministic stream supplied by the SDK.

SpaceTimeDB replaces `Math.random` in module runtimes. In guarded development
runs, `effect-spacetimedb` also replaces it with a throwing guard so accidental
callers fail loudly in tests and CI. The runtime still installs a deterministic
fallback as a non-semantic backstop for stray library paths, but application
logic should not depend on it.

The SDK random stream is deterministic and replica-reproducible. Supplying a
developer-chosen seed makes results more reproducible, not more secret.

## Strength

Reducer randomness is useful for gameplay-grade choices: shuffles, loot rolls,
procedural content, and reproducible simulations. It is not appropriate for
secrets, tokens, authentication, anti-cheat, or any security-sensitive value.

If a value must be unpredictable, generate it outside the deterministic reducer
with a trusted source of entropy and pass it in as an argument.

## Rules

- Use `Random.*` from `effect/Random` inside server handlers.
- Use context randomness only at low-level interop boundaries.
- Never use `Math.random` for server semantics.
- Never use ambient wall-clock reads for committed server semantics.
- Treat reducer randomness as deterministic and non-cryptographic.


---

# Source: /the-effect-layer/runtime-model

---
draft: false
title: Runtime Model
description: How Effect programs run inside SpaceTimeDB's synchronous, deterministic module host.
sidebar:
  order: 1
---

SpaceTimeDB runs module code inside a strict host contract: each reducer,
procedure, view, HTTP handler, and lifecycle handler is synchronous,
run-to-completion, single-transaction where applicable, and deterministic.
`effect-spacetimedb` runs Effect programs inside that contract rather than
pretending the module runtime is a normal JavaScript environment.

## Synchronous Effects Only

:::caution

Handler effects must complete in one synchronous pass. Do not use promises,
`async` functions, timers, `queueMicrotask`, or `Effect.sleep` in server module
handlers. Development guards make these operations fail loudly so code that
would suspend the module host is caught early.

:::

Finalizers from scoped Effects still run synchronously before the host commits or
rolls back, so `Effect.acquireRelease` is safe when the acquired resource is
bounded to the current call.

At the host boundary, each reducer, procedure, view, HTTP handler, and lifecycle
handler is executed with the sync runner and `Scheduler.PreventSchedulerYield`.
Anything that suspends the fiber surfaces as `HandlerAsyncNotAllowedDefect`.
`Effect.sleep` dies with the same error in all modes, so no `catch` can swallow
it. A zero-length sleep passes, so `retry` and `repeat` without a delay work.
Guarded development runs also replace timer and microtask globals with throwing
stubs so accidental use fails before a module is published.

The body of `Tx.run` runs in a fiber of its own, because the host takes it as a
synchronous callback. That fiber keeps its caller's context: services provided
around the call, log annotations and the current span all carry over. The
transaction's own services, its clock and its randomness replace the caller's.

## Determinism

Every replica must replay the same input log to the same state. Use
`Random.*` from `effect/Random` for deterministic randomness and use the call
timestamp for time. Do not call `Math.random`, `Date.now`, or
`performance.now` for server semantics. See
[Randomness & Determinism](/the-effect-layer/randomness-and-determinism) for
the full guard and UUID-helper contract.

Determinism is reproducibility, not secrecy. Generate tokens, secrets, and
cryptographically unpredictable values outside the reducer and pass them in.

The server runtime wires `Random.*` from `effect/Random` to `ctx.random`. It also
provides the Effect clock from `ctx.timestamp`, so `Effect.Clock` and
`DateTime.now` reflect the transaction timestamp. In guarded development runs,
`Math.random`, `Date.now()`, and no-argument `new Date()` throw deterministic
runtime errors; explicit conversions such as `new Date(123)`, `Date.parse`, and
`Date.UTC` remain available.

## Transactions

Reducers run inside one ambient writable transaction and may yield `Db`
directly. Procedures and HTTP handlers open transactions explicitly with `Tx` or
`HttpTx`. Transaction bodies may be retried after optimistic commit conflicts,
so keep them pure database work and put external side effects outside them.

Only mutable transactions exist in the JavaScript host. SpaceTimeDB exposes no
read-only transaction for procedures; a read-only transaction would be a
type-level convention, not a host feature. A procedure that opens several
transactions has no automatic rollback across them, so multi-step workflows need
their own status rows and cleanup process.

## Host Call Failures

Table reads and deletes return Effects with error type `never`. This includes
index lookups and streams. A broken host operation or an undecodable stored row
dies with `StdbTableOperationDefect`. Its `table`, `op` and `cause` identify
the failing operation. A missing row is a normal result. `findOrFail` uses the
error its caller supplies for that result.

Inserts and updates can fail with `StdbUniqueAlreadyExistsError` on a unique
constraint, `StdbAutoIncOverflowError` on a sequence, or
`StdbScheduleDelayTooLongError` on a scheduled table. Updating a missing row
fails with `StdbNoSuchRowError`. Each carries the operation and original cause.
An oversized outbox insert can also fail with `OutboxRowTooLargeError`.
Outside table operations, a host call such as a transaction can still fail with
`StdbHostCallError`. A transaction propagates the typed errors from its body.

The classifier uses native error class names rather than `instanceof`, because
ordinary server runtime files cannot value-import `spacetimedb/server` without
loading the host-only syscall surface. Dependency bumps should re-check the
native server error-name surface.

## Observability

Tracing is disabled on the server. Effect spans are not exported from a reducer,
and the default tracer would allocate span ids from ambient randomness, so
server effects run with tracing off. `Effect.fn` still works; it produces a noop
span.

`Effect.log*` bridges to the host console through the runtime logger. Logs
emitted while a reducer, procedure, HTTP handler, view, or lifecycle handler runs
carry the module, handler, and kind. Caller-scoped handlers also annotate the
sender identity; anonymous views and HTTP handlers omit sender.

## Polyfills And Guarded Mode

SpaceTimeDB's module runtime is a minimal JavaScript environment. The server
compat layer installs small shims only when they are missing:

- a deterministic `Math.random` fallback, used only as a library backstop,
- immediate-execution timer shims and no-op clear functions.

Module entrypoints import `effect-spacetimedb/server-compiler`, which installs
the server compatibility polyfills before exposing `build`. Native
`spacetime build` preserves that side-effectful compiler entrypoint.

The constrained runtime has a production mode and a guarded development mode.
Guarded mode is selected automatically under tests and temporarily swaps
forbidden globals for throwing stubs for the duration of each call, restoring
them afterward. Code that passes guarded mode behaves deterministically in the
host.

## Quick Rules

- Keep handler bodies synchronous.
- Use `Random.*` from `effect/Random`, not `Math.random`.
- Use call timestamps, not ambient clocks.
- Write directly in reducers; use `tx.run(...)` in procedures and HTTP handlers.
- Keep transaction bodies idempotent and database-only.
- Import `effect-spacetimedb/server-compiler` in module entrypoints; it installs
  the server polyfills without a separate bundle prelude injection.


---

# Source: /the-effect-layer/upgrading-from-0-8

---
title: Upgrading from 0.8 to 0.9
description: Upgrade the toolchain, migrate contracts and clients, and regenerate bindings.
sidebar:
  order: 9
---

## Install the matching tools

Use Node `^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1`, Effect `^4.1.1`, and SpacetimeDB **2.16.1** for the JavaScript SDK, CLI and database host. Even a module that uses default storage emits the new table-cache schema section.

1. Install `effect-spacetimedb@0.9.0` and pin `spacetimedb@2.16.1` in both the module and client projects.
2. Replace the SDK 2.14 patch with the [2.16.1 patch](https://github.com/miragegame/effect-spacetimedb/blob/v0.9.0/patches/spacetimedb@2.16.1.patch). It fixes comparisons of object-valued range keys, unique index classification and branded primitive builder inputs.
3. Configure your package manager to apply the patch and reinstall. For Bun, put the following entry in the root `package.json`. For pnpm, place the same mapping under `pnpm.patchedDependencies` or in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Other installers need an equivalent patch step.

```json
{
  "patchedDependencies": {
    "spacetimedb@2.16.1": "patches/spacetimedb@2.16.1.patch"
  }
}
```

## Update contracts and handlers

Import the root with `import * as Stdb from "effect-spacetimedb"`. For example, declare a reducer with `Stdb.Fn.reducer`, add it to `Stdb.Group.make("Users")`, then add the group to `Stdb.Module.make("app")`.

| Previous spelling | Current spelling or replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `StdbFn` | `Fn` |
| `StdbGroup` | `Group` |
| `StdbModule` | `Module` |
| `StdbHttp` | `Http` |
| `StdbHttpGroup` | `HttpGroup` |
| `StdbBuilder` | `Builder` |
| `AnyStdbModule` | `AnyModule` |
| `StdbBuildPlan` | `BuildPlan` |
| `StdbValueType` | `ValueType` |
| `StdbDiagnostic` | `Diagnostic` |
| `StdbDiagnosticSeverity` | `DiagnosticSeverity` |
| `StdbDiagnosticCode` | `DiagnosticCode` |
| `StdbTypeDescriptor` | `TypeDescriptor` |
| `StdbHostFailure` | `HostFailure` |

Remove `public` from reducers, procedures and views. Client-callable functions were already reachable on the host. For a restricted read, use a private table and a procedure that checks the sender. Tables keep their visibility setting. Scheduled, lifecycle and settle functions stay outside the projected client.

Replace a column’s `.name("display_name")` with `.columnName("display_name")`. Use `.named("UserView")` to name a generated struct type. Check existing column names before republishing because correcting a mistaken column name changes the stored schema.

An integer column can use `.autoInc()` with or without a primary key. Remove workarounds that treated chained field options as optional values. A zero on update also requests the next sequence value. Optional columns cannot carry a sequence.

Other removed names and members:

| 0.8 | 0.9 |
| --- | --- |
| `Stdb.enumType(...)` | `Stdb.enum(...)` |
| `Builder.groupChecked(...)` | `Builder.group(...)`, or `groupPrechecked(...)` for a record already annotated `GroupCheckedHandlers` |
| `LifecycleKeys` from `/server` | `LifecycleName` from the root |
| `StdbEventContextType`, `StdbReducerOutcomeType` from `/client` | `StdbEventContext`, `StdbReducerOutcome`, which are types as well as values |
| `WsSubscriptionHandleLike` from `/client` | `SubscriptionHandleLike` |
| `db.table.key.replace(...)` | `db.table.key.update(...)` |
| `db.table.index.deleteAll(...)` | `db.table.index.delete(...)` |
| the handler context's deprecated `identity` | `ctx.databaseIdentity` |
| `WaitUntilOptions.interval` | removed; `waitUntil` is event-driven and never read it |

Use `Stdb.Builder.group` for implementations and `build(module, implementations)` from `effect-spacetimedb/server-compiler` for the module entry. Replace `Server.make`, `ServerInstance`, `MakeOptions` and their single-handler and transaction helpers with module accessors. A `SyncRunner` provides `runSync` and `runSyncExit`. Remove calls to `dispose` and references to `SyncRunnerLike` or `StdbServerDisposedError`. Use `toSyncRunner` to adapt a context.

## Update clients and time limits

| Previous spelling | Current spelling or replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `makeWsClient` | `wsMake` |
| `generatedConnection` | `wsGeneratedConnection` |
| `sessionTag` | `wsSessionTag` |
| `connectAndSubscribe` | `wsConnectAndSubscribe` |
| `supervisedSessionAtom` | `wsSupervisedSessionAtom` |
| `tableAtomFamily` | `wsTableAtomFamily` |
| `rowAtomFamily` | `wsRowAtomFamily` |
| `tableGroupAtomFamily` | `wsTableGroupAtomFamily` |
| `tableGroupSnapshotAtom` | `wsTableGroupSnapshotAtom` |
| `connectTimeoutMillis` | `connectDurationMax` |
| `reconnectDelayMillisFirst` | `reconnectDelayFirst` |
| `reconnectDelayMillisMax` | `reconnectDelayMax` |
| `stabilityWindowMillis` | `stabilityWindow` |
| `delayMillisMin` | `delayMin` |
| `delayMillisMax` | `delayMax` |
| `connectTimeoutMillisDefault` | `connectDurationMaxDefault` |
| `reconnectDelayMillisFirstDefault` | `reconnectDelayFirstDefault` |
| `reconnectDelayMillisMaxDefault` | `reconnectDelayMaxDefault` |
| `stabilityWindowMillisDefault` | `stabilityWindowDefault` |

Change `client.Users.reducers.userUpsert` to `client.groups.Users.reducers.userUpsert`. The same path works on WebSocket sessions, including a session delivered by a supervisor or atom. Each group is created on first access and retains its identity. Its functions and their `.raw` variants are the same objects available under the flat `reducers` and `procedures` records. HTTP groups also have `httpHandlers`. A scoped HTTP client from `project(module).client.http.group("Users", config)` already represents one group. Names such as `cache`, `identity` and `groups` are valid group ids.

Time options accept Effect `Duration.Input`. A number still means milliseconds. Calls and connection acquisition default to 30 seconds. Set `callDurationMax` or `connectDurationMax` to `Duration.infinity` to disable that timer. A WebSocket call that exceeds its deadline ends the connection and fails with `ConnectionLostError`. Its outcome is unknown. Set the deadline above the longest expected operation. The procedure HTTP adapter also accepts a duration as its `timeout`.

The supervisor defaults to an initial delay of 250 milliseconds and a ceiling and stability window of 30 seconds each. A short-lived connection continues the previous backoff. The delay resets after a connection stays live for the stability window. Delays must be finite and nonnegative, and the stability window must be finite and positive.

Use `CallFailure<E>` and `RawCallFailure<E>` for HTTP. On WebSocket calls use `WsCallFailure<E>` or `RawWsCallFailure<E>`. Remove HTTP recovery arms for `ConnectionLostError`, `CallNotSentError` and `ConnectionIdentityChangedError`. If you construct `SubscriptionInvalidatedError` in a test, supply its `kind`. A custom `TableAtomSession` must implement `isRevoked()` and `rowsOwner()`.

## Update server failure handling

Server table reads, streams, index lookups and deletes have error type `never`. A missing `find` result is `undefined`. `findOrFail` fails with the error you supply. Remove `catchTag`, retry and `orDie` around table operations whose error channel is now empty. An unexpected host call or malformed stored row dies with `StdbTableOperationDefect`. Import the class from `effect-spacetimedb/server` and inspect its `table`, `op` and `cause` in a defect observer. Client-side decoding still reports `StdbDecodeError` for malformed data received from the server.

| Table operation | Typed failures |
| --- | --- |
| Insert, bulk insert, schedule | `StdbUniqueAlreadyExistsError` for unique constraints, `StdbAutoIncOverflowError` for sequences and `StdbScheduleDelayTooLongError` for scheduled tables |
| Primary-key update | The applicable write errors above plus `StdbNoSuchRowError` |
| Outbox insert | Applicable insert errors plus `OutboxRowTooLargeError` for the configured byte bound |
| Read, delete, clear | None |

`withTx` and scoped transaction helpers propagate the body's typed errors. The host transaction can also fail. A transaction no longer adds a decode error of its own. Its scope closes before commit and it inherits caller-provided services and log annotations. A finalizer that dies aborts the transaction. Keep external side effects outside a transaction body because the host can retry it.

Update error class imports, string tags and pattern matches together. Local class names change independently of stored rows and declared wire errors.

| Previous spelling | Current spelling or replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `OutboxRowTooLarge` | `OutboxRowTooLargeError` |
| `HttpCallDurationExceeded` | `HttpCallDurationExceededError` |
| `HttpDeclaredErrorDefinitionMissing` | `HttpDeclaredErrorDefinitionMissingDefect` |
| `InvalidRawHttpResponse` | `InvalidRawHttpResponseDefect` |
| `StdbSenderFailure` | `StdbSenderError` |
| `StdbDeclaredErrorEncodingFailure` | `StdbDeclaredErrorEncodingError` |
| `WsSessionSupervisorDefectError` | `WsSessionSupervisorFatalError` |
| `ReducerAsyncNotAllowedError` | `HandlerAsyncNotAllowedDefect` |
| `ReducerGlobalRandomNotAllowedError` | `HandlerGlobalRandomNotAllowedDefect` |
| `ReducerWallClockNotAllowedError` | `HandlerWallClockNotAllowedDefect` |
| `CallableInterruptedError` | `CallableInterruptedDefect` |
| `RuntimeLayerAsyncError` | `RuntimeLayerAsyncDefect` |
| `StdbDbSchemaMismatchError` | `StdbDbSchemaMismatchDefect` |
| `NestedTestTransactionError` | `NestedTestTransactionDefect` |
| `StdbHostAbiCapabilityError` | `StdbHostAbiCapabilityDefect` |
| `StdbHttpProjectionError` | `StdbHttpProjectionDefect` |
| `StdbFieldOptionsVersionError` | `StdbFieldOptionsVersionDefect` |
| `StdbValidationError` | `StdbValidationDefect` |
| `StdbTypeIdentifierError` | `StdbTypeIdentifierDefect` |
| `StdbTypeNotNameableError` | `StdbTypeNotNameableDefect` |
| `StdbTypeLoweringError` | `StdbTypeLoweringDefect` |
| `UnsupportedStdbTypeError` | `UnsupportedStdbTypeDefect` |
| `SatsTypeNameCollisionError` | `SatsTypeNameCollisionDefect` |
| `TestModuleEnvironmentError` | `TestModuleEnvironmentDefect` |
| `ServerPolyfillInstallError` | `ServerPolyfillInstallDefect` |
| `ServerDevGuardInstallError` | `ServerDevGuardInstallDefect` |

## Publish the module and regenerate its client

Coordinate the module and client upgrade. **Every client-callable procedure now returns an `ok` or `err` envelope**, including procedures with no declared errors. A raw success is `[0, value]`. A raw failure is `[1, carrier]`. The carrier is a string containing either the declared error payload or a version 1 `UndeclaredFailure` with a reason and message. A 0.8 client cannot decode the new result from a formerly unwrapped procedure.

```sh
spacetime generate --lang typescript --module-path . --out-dir src/module_bindings --yes
```

The typed client decodes undeclared procedure failures as `RemoteRejectedError`. Bad arguments receive status 400 with a message capped at 1,024 characters. A handler failure or result encoding failure receives status 500 with a fixed message. The module logs the underlying cause. Reducers reject invalid caller arguments with a sender error. Scheduled procedures return unit.

Pass `onDefect` to `build(module, impls, { onDefect })`. Remove the trailing observer argument from `provideConstrainedServerSupport` and `provideConstrainedServerRuntime`. An observer receives the cause once for each undeclared failure, including unexpected host errors and async work inside a synchronous handler. Zero-length sleeps complete synchronously. A positive sleep in a synchronous handler dies.

## Update test helpers and imports

A procedure bound with `bindCallables` answers with `{ ok }` or `{ err }`. Assert on the answer. Use `bindCallables(module, impls, { onDefect })` to inspect the cause. Bound calls take already-decoded arguments and return unencoded results. Test wire codecs against a host. Relative bundle paths passed to `makeDevServer` resolve from the current directory.

| Was on `./testing` | Import from |
| --- | --- |
| `project`, `AnyModuleSpec`, `TableRow`, `TypeOf`, `StdbHostEncodeError` | `effect-spacetimedb` |
| `CallFailure`, `RawCallFailure`, `WsCallFailure`, `RawWsCallFailure`, `DomainCallError`, `RemoteRejectedError`, `TransportError`, `StdbDecodeError`, `ConnectionLostError`, `catchRawTags`, `SubscriptionFailure`, `WsConnectError`, `WsConnectTimeoutError`, the stream overflow errors and buffer options | `effect-spacetimedb` or `effect-spacetimedb/client` |
| `decodeStdbEventContext`, `decodeStdbEventContextSync`, `StdbEventContext`, `StdbReducerOutcome`, `wsGeneratedConnection` and the `Generated*` types, the `Subscription*` errors, `SubscriptionHandleLike`, `TableGroup`, `TableGroupSnapshot`, `TableChange`, `TableChangeWithContext`, `WaitUntilTimeoutError`, `WaitUntilOptions`, `unsubscribeThen`, the `WsSessionSupervisor*` types, `reconnectDelayFirstDefault`, `reconnectDelayMaxDefault` | `effect-spacetimedb/client` |
| `provideConstrainedServerSupport` | `effect-spacetimedb/server` |

Each public entry exports the types needed for its signatures. Keep using `Stdb.dbCodec`, `Stdb.httpCodec` and `Stdb.wsCodec` for transport interoperation. Use `Stdb.reflect` or module accessors for contract metadata. Use session refs and the subscription helpers for cache access.

| Removed operation | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `declOf`, `encodeCallArgs`, `isUnitValueType`, `outboxTargetIndexName`, `wireNameForDecl`, `wireNameOf` | Inspect the module or use its projected calls |
| `canonicalizeTableGroupKeys`, `canonicalRowKey`, `canonicalTableGroupKey`, `canonicalTableKey`, `canonicalValueKey`, `subscribeSnapshotRef` | `subscribeRowRef`, `subscribeTableRef`, `subscribeTableGroupRef` |
| `httpGroupFromModulePlan`, `layerFromModulePlan`, `wsSupervisorFromModulePlan` | Construct clients from `Stdb.project(module).client` |
| `RemoteRejectedBody` | Handle `RemoteRejectedError` with its raw response and status |

Three more names changed.

| Previous spelling | Current spelling or replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `timestampAddMillis` | `timestampAdd` |
| `StdbBuilder.plan` | Use `build(module, implementations)` in module entries and `bindCallables(module, implementations)` in tests. |
| `RESERVED_GROUP_CLIENT_KEYS` | Removed. Only JavaScript prototype member names remain reserved as group ids. |

## Additions and defaults

- Choose `required_in_memory`, `required_on_disk` or `no_requirement` through a table's `cachePolicy` or the module's `settings.tableCachePolicyDefault`. The default is in memory. Disk-capable policies require btree indexes. Republish a policy change in place with existing rows and bindings.
- Mount an Effect module with `.mount(key, Library)` and `Builder.mount`, or a native SDK library with `.mountNative<Library>()(key)` and its native implementation. Use `mounts[key].run` for an Effect library and `mounts[key].use` for a native callback. Effect mounts expose nested calls, tables, subscription targets and cache reads. All mounts share the parent database and transaction. An optional `{ name }` pins the wire namespace. The maximum depth is four. Declare environment, HTTP routes, lifecycle hooks and inter-database receivers on the root.
- Array length bounds are optional. `Stdb.array(item)` has no length check. Supply `minimum`, `maximum` or both when needed. When inspecting `Stdb.describe(type).length`, either bound can be absent.
- Table deltas and event inserts retain every change by default. An explicit `bufferSize` bounds memory and signals overflow. Table delta subscribers can also opt into sliding or dropping. Snapshot notifications coalesce because a snapshot reads current rows.
- Table, column, index and callable declarations accept snake_case and preserve authored names at the Effect boundary. Use a plain string schema when your domain has no additional string constraint.
- An undecodable server message invalidates the affected WebSocket cache and parks a supervisor by default. A normal connection loss preserves the last rows for the same identity. A changed identity or failed token refresh revokes them. Keep a token across reconnects when the client should retain its identity.
- `IdcPump.drain({ deliveriesMax })` defaults to 1,000 deliveries. A refused connection stops the pump, and exhausting the bound with pending rows raises `RangeError`.
